name: Jeune Syndrome (Asphyxiating Thoracic Dystrophy)

criteria.description: Narrow, bell-shaped thorax with short ribs
Shortened long bones (rhizomelic or mesomelic limb shortening)
Respiratory distress or insufficiency due to thoracic restriction
Presence of renal cystic disease or nephronophthisis
Identification of pathogenic variants in known causative genes (e.g., IFT80, DYNC2H1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (narrow thorax, short limbs, respiratory insufficiency) with or without supportive genetic or minor clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical presentation is key.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic thoracic deformity causing respiratory compromise

pathognomonic.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to thoracic restriction
pathognomonic.notes: Often presents in neonatal period or early infancy

common.notes: Extra digits on hands or feet
May develop in infancy or childhood
Variable severity, may contribute to morbidity
Secondary to skeletal abnormalities and respiratory issues

occasional.notes: Progressive vision impairment in some cases
Including septal defects or valve abnormalities

rare.notes: Severe renal involvement in rare cases
Developmental delay or intellectual disability in rare severe cases

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine or markers of renal dysfunction in advanced cases
imaging: Chest X-ray showing narrow, bell-shaped thorax with short ribs
Skeletal survey demonstrating shortened long bones
MRI or CT may show hepatic fibrosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in IFT80, DYNC2H1, WDR19, or other ciliopathy-related genes
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern
Histopathology of liver or kidney may show fibrosis or cystic changes

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonatal period
Signs of hepatic failure or portal hypertension
references: Beales PL, et al. Asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (Jeune syndrome): clinical and molecular genetics. J Med Genet. 2007.
McInerney-Leo AM, et al. Short-rib polydactyly and Jeune syndromes are caused by mutations in WDR19. Am J Hum Genet. 2013.
